next.name: Kinsing
next.headline: Kinsing: a Monero-mining campaign that hunts exposed cloud services
next.in_short: Kinsing has been active since 2019. It breaks into misconfigured or unpatched cloud-native services, then runs a Monero miner. Researchers disagree on what Kinsing is, and they name no sponsor.

sentences.t: The catalogue lists Money Libra as another name for Kinsing.
Aqua Nautilus says Kinsing first surfaced as a threat in 2019. It says its own Docker API honeypot took the first known attack on December 15, 2019.

Aqua Nautilus says TrustedSec was first to report on Kinsing, on January 15, 2020. Alibaba Cloud's security team followed a day later and called it h2Miner. Aqua says it named the malware Kinsing in April 2020.
Aqua Nautilus says it found no single answer on whether Kinsing is one threat actor, a malware name or leaked source code.
Aqua says infrastructure choices may suggest a link to Russian-speaking countries, which could imply Russian origins. It presents this as a possibility, not a finding.
Aqua Nautilus says the campaign targets 75 different applications. It reports that 91% are open source and 67% are runtime applications. It also lists CI/CD tools such as Jenkins.
Aqua says its Shodan search found 2.5 million instances of the applications Kinsing targets.
Sysdig describes Kinsing going after misconfigured cloud-native environments and exposed Docker engines.
Trend Micro's Redis honeypot captures included Kinsing. They show how Redis instances left open without authentication can be abused for remote code execution.
Aqua Nautilus says Kinsing typically exploits vulnerable or misconfigured applications and runs an infection script. It then runs a Monero cryptominer, often hidden by a rootkit.
According to Aqua, the scripts stop and delete security tools such as SELinux, Aegis and AppArmor. Its analysis found the first script type mainly aims at eliminating competition.
Sysdig reports that Kinsing's miner, called kdevtmpfsi, ran in the /tmp directory of its honeypot. Kinsing contacted command-and-control servers, downloaded more scripts and spread using SSH keys.
Trend Micro reports the Redis sample installed the XMRig Monero miner under the name kdevtmpfsi. It also reports persistence through cron.
Sysdig says a security researcher reported that Kinsing is written in Golang.

Aqua Nautilus says Kinsing adds new vulnerabilities soon after their release. Its list includes CVE-2019-19781 (Citrix NetScaler), CVE-2020-7961 (Liferay), CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) and CVE-2022-26134 (Confluence).
A 2020 round-up of Go malware reports that Alibaba Cloud researchers first reported Kinsing in January 2020. It also says Kinsing was seen exploiting CVE-2020-11651 in May of that year.
Aqua says its honeypots were targeted by Kinsing eight times a day on average.

In a post dated September 14, 2022, Trend Micro described Kinsing being deployed through the older Oracle WebLogic flaw CVE-2020-14882. A crafted request led to a script that disabled security features and removed rival miners.
FortiGuard Labs reported on November 28, 2023 that Kinsing was among several malware families delivered through the Apache ActiveMQ flaw CVE-2023-46604. The report names no attacker group.
A December 2022 vendor report on a Linux cryptojacking attack says the original routine terminated competing malware such as Kinsing.
Patch internet-facing services quickly. Keep Docker, Redis and similar services behind authentication and off the open internet.
